column1: # vdi-raster-screen.tsv -- the VDI raster group with the SCREEN as an operand.
# Read by DUMPRAST (core/dumprast.c), area 6, record 3696 bytes -- the same
# record as vdi-raster.tsv.  Loader, column format, the geometry guard and
# the three additions this table uses (!screen, S, preludes, readback):
# core/cases.h, "THE SCREEN".  Spec: docs/api/vdi/raster/_raster.md.
#   opcode <TAB> intin <TAB> ptsin <TAB> src <TAB> dst <TAB> fill <TAB> comment
# src/dst = buffer,fd_w,fd_h,fd_wdwidth,fd_stand,fd_nplanes, or S for the
# screen (fd_addr NULL, every other field 0).  fill = seed_a,seed_b, or
# seed_a,seed_b,rx,ry,rw,rh: after the call the runner reads the screen
# rectangle back with v_get_pixel into buffer B, row * 32 + col, so the
# record carries it where buffer B always is.  A '+' line is a prelude:
# issued after the reset, before the measured call, never recorded.
# WHY A SCREEN OPERAND IS COMPARABLE NOW, AND ON WHAT
# vdi-raster.tsv has no screen MFDB because the TT's screen (4 planes) and
# NewTOS' (16) meant different words.  The reference for THIS table is
# EmuTOS 1.4 on a Falcon030 in VIDEL truecolor (Hatari, 640x480, 16 planes,
# EMUDESK.INF "#E 1A E0 00 1C 60"), which is the device model NewTOS runs
# in QEMU raspi4b: every screen word is the Falcon 16-bit pixel
# RRRRRGGGGGOBBBBB (O = OVERLAY_BIT 0x0020, vdi_fill.c:26).  The table
# declares that screen and the runner refuses a smaller or shallower one.
# THE WORDS THIS TABLE EXPECTS, all from EmuTOS
#   cleared screen  0xFFFF  v_clrwk memsets 0xff (vdi_control.c:610-618)
#   pen 0 white     0xFFDF  set_color16: (r<<11)|(g<<6)|b, 5-bit guns
#                           (vdi_col.c:588-613); bit 5 is never set
#   pen 1 black     0x0000  pen 2 red 0xF800  pen 3 green 0x07C0
#   pen 4 blue      0x001F  pen 6 yellow 0xFFC0  pen 8 (733,733,733)
#   0xBDD7  pen 9 (533,533,533) 0x8C51  (videl_palette1, vdi_col.c:130)
#   pen 16 = videl_palette2[0] white 0xFFDF, pen 255 = [239] black 0x0000
#   vdi2fivebits: (col*31+500)/1000 (vdi_col.c:588-591)
#   v_get_pixel on a truecolor screen: INTOUT[0] = 0, INTOUT[1] = the word
#   (vdi_fill.c:671-681, 1095-1110); the readback stores INTOUT[1].
# A memory MFDB at 16 planes is one UWORD per pixel on both machines
# (vro_cpyfm16 / vrt_cpyfm16, vdi_raster.c:975-1326); the buffers are laid
# with td_rast_fill (record.c), every word different.
# The reset before every case (runner.c, td_reset_vdi) clears the screen
# with v_clrwk and sets vs_clip off, vsf_interior solid, vsf_color 1: that
# is the defined state every case starts from, and the restore of whatever
# the previous case drew.  There is no bb_save-style copy back.
# PREDICTED DIFFERENCES, made before the run, both marked below:
#   * H12 (vrt_cpyfm, PAT_FLAG|MD_REPLACE on the 16-bit path): EmuTOS'
#     vrt_cpyfm16 re-reads the unstripped INTIN[0] and returns on 0x11
#     (vdi_raster.c:1236, 1325-1326) -- nothing drawn.  NewTOS strips
#     PAT_FLAG and draws (raster.rs, vrt_cpyfm).  D-VDI-23's "unmeasured
#     twin" in _raster.md, measurable on a Falcon.
#   * none for vro_cpyfm: the 16-bit PAT_FLAG rule is already reproduced
#     (raster.rs, vro_cpyfm; vdi-raster.tsv case 144).
!screen
# SECTION E -- R02: vro_cpyfm (109) SCREEN -> MEMORY.
# Source S, destination buffer B as a 32x16 form at 16 planes (512 words,
# the whole buffer).  EmuTOS: setup_info takes v_bas_ad/v_planes/v_lin_wr
# for the source (vdi_raster.c:925-929), s_nxwd = d_nxwd = 32 so the copy
# runs (:1360), vro_cpyfm16 applies the op word by word (:975-1221).
# No clipping: the destination is not the screen (:947-949).
# E1: the cleared screen -- OVL-001 consequence (2): 512 words 0xFFFF.

column7: E1 cleared screen to memory: 512 x 0xFFFF
E2 cleared screen at the origin to memory

column1: # the op runs in the 16-bit domain on the whole word, overlay bit included
# a vr_recfl pen fill (solid, replace, after the reset) then read back:
# the pen's word, not the reference's palette index.

column7: E8 pen 2 fill to memory: 512 x 0xF800
E9 partial pen 3 fill: rows 4-11 cols 8-23 0x07C0, rest 0xFFFF

column1: # pen 0 is 0xFFDF, the cleared screen 0xFFFF: OVERLAY_BIT alone

column7: E10 pen 0 fill to memory: 512 x 0xFFDF, not 0xFFFF

column1: # a memory destination anchor off the origin: d_xmin/d_ymin and the
# memory stride (d_nxln = fd_wdwidth * 32, :938)

column7: E11 16x8 pen 4 block to memory (8,4): 0x001F there, fill elsewhere

column1: # two pens whose guns are not 0 or 31: the 5-bit quantisation
# the rules on the screen path

column7: E13 destination 4 planes: s_nxwd 32 != d_nxwd 8, no-op (:1360)
E14 PAT_FLAG|3 on the 16-bit path: nothing copied (:980, D-VDI-23)
E15 reversed source corners: sorted copy, PTSIN unchanged (D-VDI-24)
E18 XOR a red screen into the fill: B = fill ^ 0xF800

column1: # SECTION F -- R03: vro_cpyfm (109) MEMORY -> SCREEN, read back.
# Source buffer A (32x16, 16 planes), destination S.  EmuTOS: d_form =
# v_bas_ad, plane_ct = v_planes = 16 (:940-944); clipping only if vs_clip
# is on (:947-949) -- the reset turns it off, so dont_clip (:882-900).
# The readback window (100,60) 32x16 is the destination rectangle, or
# a larger window so an over-draw at the border would show as a word
# that is not 0xFFFF.

column7: F1 the whole form to the screen: readback = fill(31)
F2 16x8 from (8,4) to (101,61): rows 1-8 cols 1-16, 0xFFFF border
F3 XOR onto the cleared screen: ~fill
F9 ALL_BLACK: 0xFFFF, indistinguishable from the cleared screen
F11 PAT_FLAG|3 on the 16-bit path: nothing drawn, 0xFFFF

column1: # clipping, destination screen (do_clip, :809-877): the visible part
# keeps its source offset -- s_xmin moves with d_xmin (:824-826)

column7: F13 clipped to (104,62)-(127,73): fill inside, 0xFFFF outside
vs_clip on, cutting right and bottom
F14 clip ends at (115,67): cols 0-15 rows 0-7 only
F15 reversed destination corners: lands at (100,60) (arb_corner)
F20 source at (5,3), not word aligned: fill[(3+r)*32+5+c]

column1: # SECTION G -- R04: vro_cpyfm (109) SCREEN -> SCREEN, overlapping.
# A prelude lays a 16x8 block of the fill at the source rectangle; the
# case moves it by (8,4), (8,0) or (0,4) in each direction so that the
# destination overlaps the source.  EmuTOS chooses the copy direction by
# comparing the two START ADDRESSES (vro_cpyfm16, :993): src < dst ->
# start at s_xmax/s_ymax and d_xmax/d_ymax, step -1 (:994-999).  On one
# screen that is: reverse iff the destination is lower, or on the same
# row and further right.  NewTOS decides rows and columns separately
# (vdi_backend.rs, copy_rect: down = dy > sy, right = dx > sx); for a
# screen the two rules give the same picture -- which this section
# measures rather than argues.  Every word of the fill differs, so a
# copy that eats itself is visible.  PTSIN[6..7] is always consistent
# with the source extent (D-VDI-25 / R01 is deferred and not restated).

column7: G1 down and right by (8,4): backwards path
G2 up and left by (8,4): forwards path
G3 right by 8, same rows: backwards, column order decides
G4 left by 8, same rows: forwards
G5 down by 4, same columns: backwards, row order decides
G6 up by 4, same columns: forwards
G7 down and left: backwards rows, EmuTOS also backwards columns
G8 up and right: forwards rows, EmuTOS also forwards columns

column1: # XOR over the overlap: an earlier write is read back as source later
# only if the directions differ, so the picture is the direction

column7: G11 onto itself: src == dst, forwards, unchanged
G12 XOR onto itself: 0x0000 over the block
G14 down and right, clipped to (104,62)-(127,73)
G16 PAT_FLAG|3 screen to screen: nothing copied
G17 to the origin, far apart: the block at (0,0), 0xFFFF border

column1: # SECTION H -- R05: vrt_cpyfm (121) MONO -> SCREEN, read back.
# Source buffer A as a 1-plane 32x16 form (two words per row, MSB first,
# the fill's bits), destination S.  EmuTOS: s_nxwd == 2 (:1384), fg/bg =
# MAP_COL[validate_color_index(INTIN[1..2])] (:1390-1395), plane_ct 16 ->
# vrt_cpyfm16 (:1432-1437): fgcol = palette[fg], bgcol = palette[bg]
# (:1233-1236); MD_REPLACE fg/bg, MD_TRANS fg on set bits, MD_XOR ~word
# on set bits, MD_ERASE bg on clear bits (:1258-1323).  Expected pixels
# are the pens' words -- never the reference's palette indices.

column7: H2 MD_TRANS pen 1: set 0x0000, clear stays 0xFFFF
H3 MD_XOR on the cleared screen: set ~0xFFFF = 0x0000
H4 MD_ERASE bg pen 0: clear 0xFFDF, set stays 0xFFFF
H7 MD_ERASE bg yellow: clear 0xFFC0, set stays 0xFFFF
H8 MD_XOR on red: set ~0xF800 = 0x07FF, clear 0xF800
H9 pens out of range: validate_color_index -> 1, all 0x0000
H11 source at (5,3), not word aligned: bits (3+r, 5+c), border 0xFFFF

column1: # PREDICTED DIFFERENCE, see the head of the file

column7: H12 PAT_FLAG|MD_REPLACE on the 16-bit path: EmuTOS draws nothing
H13 the screen as a mono source: s_nxwd 32 != 2, no-op

column1: # a 16-plane MEMORY destination: vrt_cpyfm16 on memory, which the TT
# could not run (vwk->ext NULL outside truecolor, vdi_control.c:450-452)

column7: H17 MD_REPLACE into memory: set 0xF800, clear 0x001F
H18 MD_XOR into memory: set ~fill(124), clear fill(124)
